content.text:
## Verdict: **DO NOT SHIP**

I exercised `dev.lincforge.benchtarget` on a Pixel 8 Pro (Android 16) emulator. The build has severe, easily-triggered defects in its core navigation and its primary content action. Both the crash log history on the device and my own manual testing corroborate the same set of problems.

### Defect 1 — Home screen navigation is almost entirely broken (Critical)
The Home screen has four buttons: **Catalog, Form, About, Checkout**.
- **Catalog**, **Form**, and **Checkout** do nothing when tapped — verified with single taps, repeated taps, double-taps, and by polling for delayed response. They are dead buttons.
- **About** is the only button that navigates anywhere, but it opens the **Catalog** screen instead of an About screen. There is no way to reach a real About screen, and Catalog is only reachable through this misrouted button (not through its own, non-functional button).
- **Form** and **Checkout** screens appear to be completely unreachable through the UI.

This alone makes 3 of the app's 4 advertised features inaccessible to a normal user.

### Defect 2 — Catalog list rows open the wrong item's detail screen (High)
Tapping a row in the Catalog list frequently opens the `DetailScreen` for a different item than the one tapped (e.g., tapping "Item 002" opened "Item 001"; tapping the row at "Item 006"'s position opened "Item 003"). The offset was not consistent (-1 in one case, -3 in others), suggesting a stale/mismatched index being captured in the list's click handling rather than a simple fixed off-by-one — consistent with a race between touch dispatch and list recomposition. Users cannot reliably view the item they intend to select.

### Defect 3 — Fatal crash tapping "Export" on the Detail screen (Critical)
Device crash logs (captured before and independent of my session) show four fatal crashes, all identical:
```
java.lang.IllegalStateException: export buffer not initialized
  at dev.lincforge.benchtarget.core.ExportPolicy.export(ExportPolicy.kt:11)
  at dev.lincforge.benchtarget.ui.ScreensKt.DetailScreen$lambda$0$0$0(Screens.kt:90)
```
This is thrown directly from the Export button's `onClick` in `DetailScreen` (`Screens.kt:90`), calling into `ExportPolicy.export()` (`ExportPolicy.kt:11`), which assumes a buffer that isn't guaranteed to be initialized. I was not able to reproduce it live in this session (my taps landed on an already-initialized code path), which points to this being a timing/race condition — the crash logs show it occurred 4 times in a ~2 minute window on this same device, so it is real and apparently not rare in practice, not a one-off fluke.

### Additional note (lower confidence)
The accessibility/view-hierarchy dump (`mobile_list_elements_on_screen`) failed consistently on every screen of this app (`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'node')`), while it presumably works for other apps in general use. This could indicate malformed or missing semantics in the Compose tree, which would also be an accessibility defect, but I can't rule out a tooling-side issue — worth a quick manual accessibility check before shipping regardless of the other findings.

### Why this blocks shipping
- Two of the four top-level features are unreachable, and a third opens the wrong destination.
- The one feature that is reachable (Catalog → Detail) has both a data-integrity bug (wrong item shown) and a fatal crash on its primary action button.
- These are not edge cases — they are hit via the app's main, first-screen navigation.

Recommend blocking release and filing bugs against: Home screen button wiring (`Screens.kt`, Home composable), Catalog list item click/index handling (`Screens.kt`, Catalog composable), and `ExportPolicy.export()` initialization (`ExportPolicy.kt:11`).
